Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Challenges as achievements — sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements

## Problem statement

The engine's challenge system (per-run meta-goals, e.g. Main Street's "Foodie Row") is conceptually a form of achievement. Once the Steam version exists (Electron launcher with Steamworks), challenge completions should sync to Steam achievements so players earn persistent, account-level recognition visible on their Steam profile and in the overlay.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn Steam achievements for completing in-game challenges; see progress on their Steam profile.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — an engine-generic achievement layer so any game can map its challenges to Steam achievements without writing Steam SDK code.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want the challenges I complete in Main Street (and future games) to appear as Steam achievements, so my progress is recognised beyond the run itself.
- As a TCE developer, I want a game-agnostic achievement layer in the engine, so adding achievements to a new game is declarative (challenge → achievement mapping) with no Steam SDK code in the game.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An **engine-generic achievement layer** exists in the core engine (extending the existing generic `ChallengeSystem` model): games define achievement definitions (id, title, description, hidden flag) and map challenge completions to achievements. This layer is pure engine code with no Steam dependency (works headless / in the web build).
2. When a challenge is completed inside the Steam launcher, the mapped Steam achievement is unlocked via Steamworks (`ISteamUserStats::SetAchievement` + `StoreStats`); verified by automated tests with a mocked Steamworks session and a documented manual E2E check with a real Steam account.
3. Steam sync is **idempotent and offline-safe**: unlocked achievements persist locally, are re-synced to Steam when available, and the launcher never crashes when Steam/Steamworks is absent (graceful degradation, consistent with the follow-on-Steam feature CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
4. A single **achievement manifest** (game id ↔ achievement id ↔ Steam API name, hidden flag) is the source of truth and matches the static Steam store configuration; mismatch detection is documented.
5. **Main Street is the first consumer**: all 12 challenge templates (`MainStreetChallenges.ts`) are mapped to Steam achievements through the generic layer (no Steam SDK code in the game module).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Timing:** Steam sync is implemented only when the Steam version exists — blocked by the Electron launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) and the Steamworks integration introduced by the follow-on-Steam incentive (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC). The engine-generic achievement layer itself can be designed/built now; the Steam bridge lands with Steamworks.
- **Engine-generic (user decision):** no game-specific Steam code; games declare achievements via the generic layer; Main Street first.
- **Steam backend reality:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steam store backend with static API names (App ID + achievement list). The manifest must match that configuration; store setup itself lives outside this repo.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies (Steamworks SDK usage follows the pattern set by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC).
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` / `ActiveChallengeRecord<TState>` interfaces plus generic selection/evaluation; game-agnostic by design ("M6 extraction" notes already anticipate reuse).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — the only consumer: 12 challenge templates across 5 categories, per-run selection (`selectChallenges`), evaluation with completion callback that pushes to `state.challengesCompleted` and the activity log. Challenges are run-local and non-persistent.
- No achievements, no Steam SDK code, no Electron code in the repo today. Steamworks integration is being introduced by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC into the launcher from CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC explicitly defers this scope: "Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item."

## Desired change

1. Add an **achievement concept to the core engine** (new module, e.g. `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`, or an extension of `ChallengeSystem`): achievement definitions, a completion-event surface, and a persistence-agnostic "unlock" registry that the web build can use without Steam.
2. Define the **achievement manifest** for the launcher (`electron/steam-achievements.ts`): game/achievement ids ↔ Steam API names + hidden flags, documented to match the Steam store backend config.
3. Add the **Steam bridge** in the Electron main process: renderer reports achievement-unlocked events via preload/IPC; main process calls Steamworks `SetAchievement`/`StoreStats`; local persistence of unlocked ids with later re-sync; graceful degradation without Steam.
4. **Wire Main Street** as the first consumer: a declarative mapping from the 12 challenge templates to Steam achievements, fired from the existing challenge-completion path.
5. Tests (mocked Steamworks session; headless unit tests for the engine layer) + documentation (README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `AGENTS.md` as needed).

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts` (new) — generic achievement definitions + unlock registry + completion-event surface (no Steam dependency).
- `src/core-engine/index.ts` — barrel exports for the new module.
- `electron/steam-achievements.ts` (new) — achievement manifest (ids ↔ Steam API names) + Steamworks sync bridge.
- `electron/main.ts`, `electron/preload.ts` — IPC surface for achievement-unlock events from the renderer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` (or a new `MainStreetAchievements.ts`) — mapping of the 12 challenge templates to achievements.
- `tests/` — unit tests (engine layer, manifest matching) + mocked-Steamworks sync tests.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — Steam achievements workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — introduces Steamworks SDK integration into the Electron launcher; explicitly defers achievements as a follow-up; its Steamworks setup (init, app ID, mock strategy) is a prerequisite and pattern for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the "Steam version"; provides the Electron main/preload and DLC content architecture this feature plugs into.
- **CG-0MSMGKVSS000ZEDL – Achievement give-aways: unlock three games when achievements are achieved** (open, idea) — separate item that consumes this item's achievement events as unlock triggers.
- `src/core-engine/ChallengeSystem.ts` — the generic challenge model this feature generalises.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Steam version" means the Electron launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW / CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Assumption:** Steam achievements must be pre-defined on the Steamworks backend (static API names); the manifest must match that config — coordination with Steam store setup (outside repo) is required before release.
- **Risk:** Challenge completion is currently in-memory/run-local; exposing it as a durable, replayable event (via the existing transcript/event infrastructure) is needed for reliable sync — mitigation: build the completion-event surface in the engine layer first.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module packaging complexity — reuse the approach validated by CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam cloud saves, non-binary stat tracking, trading cards, and wishlist prompts are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the challenge→achievement layer be engine-generic (any game's challenges can map to Steam achievements, Main Street first) or only cover Main Street for now?" — Answer (user): "engine-generic". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: the layer is a core-engine module; Main Street is the first consumer.
- Q2: "When should the Steam sync be built?" — Answer (user): per the intake request, "when the steam version has been created these achievements should sync with Steam achievements." Implication: implementation of the Steam bridge is gated on the launcher + Steamworks items; the engine abstraction is not.
- OPEN QUESTION: The exact Steam achievement list/API names for the store backend (business/backend decision outside the repo) — the manifest defines them in one place; the store config must match.

# Intake Brief: Achievement give-aways — unlock three games when achievements are achieved

## Problem statement

To reward engaged players, three games from the TCE catalog will be given away free when players achieve certain achievements in the Steam launcher. The unlock uses the **same game-agnostic mechanism** as the free game awarded for following on Steam (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches.

## Users

- **Steam players** — earn free games as a reward for reaching achievements; a reason to keep playing.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — a growth/engagement mechanic that drives play without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want a free game to unlock in my launcher once I've won my first game and reached one more milestone, so my progress is rewarded.
- As a publisher, I want achievement give-aways delivered through the existing bundled-content/unlock architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Three games are selected** from the TCE catalog for achievement give-away; the selection is a documented business decision (Main Street is a noted candidate; selection avoids overlap with the follow-on-Steam bonus game choice — see Related work) and the chosen set + rationale is recorded in the item/design doc.
2. Each give-away game unlocks when the player achieves its configured trigger achievements: **"win your first game" plus one additional achievement** (suggested: first win in a second distinct game — final choice recorded, see Appendix). Trigger definitions live in one config (achievement ids → game id) and are game-agnostic.
3. The unlock uses **the same mechanism as the follow-on-Steam free game** (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC): bundled content, locked by default, unlocked in place, persisted across launches, game-agnostic unlock logic.
4. Unlock state persists across launches; re-checks on demand; graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent (CTA/lock state degrades without crashing the app).
5. Trigger achievements come from the engine-generic achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ): give-away config consumes achievement-unlock events, not game-specific hacks.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't reinvent:** the unlock mechanism (bundled-content unlock, persistence, game-agnostic design) is the one designed in CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC; this item adds achievement-triggered unlocks as an additional trigger source on the same path.
- **Game selection is a business decision** and part of this item's scope (user: "don't know yet (note Main Street)").
- **Dependencies:** blocked by CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (achievements exist as engine-generic events) and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (unlock mechanism). Both are prerequisites for implementation.
- **Trigger achievements:** "win your first game" plus one more (user decision; second achievement suggested — final choice to be confirmed).
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).

## Existing state

- Follow-on-Steam item (CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, intake_complete) designs the game-agnostic free-game unlock: Steamworks-based follow detection + local unlock persistence + bundled DLC content; **not yet implemented** — this item should coordinate so the unlock path is shared.
- No achievement system exists yet; CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ (challenges → Steam achievements, engine-generic) is the event source this item consumes.
- Game catalog (`main.ts` GAMES): Gym (demos), 9-Card Golf, Beleaguered Castle, Sushi Go!, Feudalism, Lost Cities, Main Street, Blackjack, Coloretto. Steam launcher (CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW) will bundle a subset with DLC architecture.
- CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC has an open question: which game is the designated free follow-bonus (business decision, game-agnostic ACs) — give-away selection must not conflict with it.

## Desired change

1. **Select and document the three give-away games** (business decision; Main Street noted as a candidate; rationale recorded).
2. Define the **trigger config** (achievement ids from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ's manifest → unlocked game id) in one place (e.g. `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts`).
3. **Extend the shared unlock mechanism** from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC to accept achievement-triggered unlocks (same persistence/unlock path; new trigger source alongside the follow trigger).
4. **UI:** locked give-away games shown in the Game Selector with unlock progress (which trigger achievements remain); unlocked games become playable.
5. Tests (mocked trigger source + unlock persistence; headless unit tests) + documentation.

## Key Files

- `electron/achievement-giveaways.ts` (new) — give-away config: trigger achievement ids → game id; selection rationale comment.
- `electron/` unlock module from CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC — extended with the achievement trigger source (shared path, game-agnostic).
- `src/ui/GameSelectorScene.ts` (or launcher UI module) — locked state + unlock progress display for give-away games.
- Achievement manifest from CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — the trigger ids referenced by the config.
- `tests/` — unit tests for trigger evaluation and unlock persistence with mocked sources.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md` — give-away configuration and QA workflow documentation.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC – Follow-on-Steam incentive: unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher** (open, intake_complete) — the unlock mechanism this item reuses; its open question on the follow-bonus game choice must be coordinated with give-away selection.
- **CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ – Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (open, idea) — the engine-generic achievement event source; blocked-by for this item.
- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, plan_complete) — the Steam version hosting both features.
- `main.ts` GAMES catalog — the candidate pool for the three give-away games.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ and CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC land first; this item's implementation is gated on both.
- **Assumption:** The three give-away games are chosen from the current catalog; Main Street is a candidate (user note).
- **Risk:** Conflict between the follow-on-Steam bonus game and the give-away set (e.g. same game twice, or devaluing the follow incentive) — mitigation: selection and rationale recorded, coordinated with the follow-item's open question.
- **Risk:** If the achievement layer (CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ) is delayed, the trigger source is missing — mitigation: define the trigger config/interface in this item early, independent of Steam sync internals.
- **Scope-creep risk:** trading cards, seasonal give-aways, paid DLC sales, and anti-abuse (achievement-farm detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Do you already have the three games in mind, or should the work item include evaluating/selecting them from the catalog (e.g. Main Street, Golf, Blackjack…)?"
  — Answer (user): "don't know yet (note Main Street)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). Implication: selection is a deliverable of this item; Main Street is a recorded candidate.
- Q2: "Should the give-away unlock on specific milestone achievements (e.g. 'complete all challenges in a game', 'win your first game'), or on any achievement being reached?"
  — Answer (user): "win your first game plus one other (suggest)". Source: interactive reply (2026-08-09). **Suggested second achievement: "win your first game in a second distinct game"** (rewards breadth of play; both triggers are engine-generic and achievable without the give-away game itself). Alternative candidates: "complete your first full game" (reach a game-over screen without quitting) or "complete all challenges in any game". Final choice to be confirmed at planning.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which three games? (business decision; Main Street noted).
- OPEN QUESTION: Final definition of the second trigger achievement (suggestion above; confirm at planning).

## Summary

The F1-approved follow-detection mechanism — `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(developerSteamID)` — is **not exposed** by `steamworks.js`, the only maintained npm binding for the Steamworks SDK (verified: v0.4.0 exposes achievement/apps/auth/cloud/input/localplayer/matchmaking/networking/overlay/stats/utils/workshop namespaces, but **no `friends` namespace**).

As a result, the launcher shipped on CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC implements:
- real SDK store-page opening via `overlay.activateToStore` / `activateToWebPage`,
- real Steamworks init (`init` + `restartAppIfNecessary` + app id bootstrap),
- follow detection **capability-detected**: `followCheckSupported = false` when the binding lacks the API, with a persisted **manual self-attest claim** fallback.

This delivers the feature with graceful degradation, but does **not** achieve fully automatic follow detection.

## Desired outcome

Automatic follow detection that survives an audit of intake AC2 ("the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks"), via one of:

- (a) A small **custom native addon** wrapping `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` (N-API), shipped alongside `steamworks.js`; the existing `SteamworksClientLike.friends.isFollowing` seam means no TypeScript change is needed once present.
- (b) A newer `steamworks.js` release (or a fork) that exposes `friends.isFollowing`.
- (c) A publisher-backend Steam Web API check (needs a server component; previously scoped out).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A concrete mechanism exposing `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` is available to the Electron main process.
- [ ] `SteamworksFollowSource.followCheckSupported` becomes `true` on a real Steam session and automatic unlock is verified end-to-end with a real Steam account.
- [ ] No regression to the graceful-degradation path (absent module → unavailable, no crash).
- [ ] Automated tests cover the new detection path with a fake module.

## Relationship

Discovered while implementing CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC (F3). Follow-up, not a blocker: the shipped feature degrades to a manual claim.

## Goal

On a **real Windows x64 machine with the Steam client**, validate end-to-end that the Option A native addon (`native/steam-friends`) enables **automatic** Steam follow detection, that the bonus game unlocks without a manual claim, and that every degradation path is safe. This is the operator-run validation for the epic **`CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1`** (implementation P1–P5 are complete on `dev`); executing this runbook produces the evidence that satisfies **P6 `CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU`** and parent AC2.

**Discovered from:** `CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1` (epic). **Complements:** P6 `CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU` (epic verification child). **Reference plan:** `docs/dev/steam-follow-qa.md`.

## What was built (the thing being validated)

Serial implementation already on `dev`:

| Item | Commit | Delivered |
|------|--------|-----------|
| P1 `CG-0MUNBHWY90051NAU` | `64367e0c` | Spike report `docs/dev/steam-follow-native-spike.md` |
| P2 `CG-0MUNBHXMC00192G8` | `b56c0ef4` | Loader seam (`nativeFriendsLoader`, `followCheckTimeoutMs`) + fake-module tests |
| P3 `CG-0MUNBHYAB0011XXW` | `1835d882` | C++ N-API addon (`native/steam-friends`) + `electron/steam-follow-native.ts` |
| P4 `CG-0MUNBHYY0001PHKU` | `fb5e5bd5` | Packaging (`electron-builder.yml`), `scripts/build-steam-friends.mjs`, `scripts/check-steam-friends.mjs`, `package:steam` |
| P5 `CG-0MUNBHZL3006UK6U` | `4d6e0aa2` | Docs, licensing, QA plan |

Mechanism: `steamworks.js` 0.4.0 exposes no `friends.isFollowing`, so the addon finds the `steam_api64.dll` **already loaded by `steamworks.js`**, calls `SteamAPI_ISteamFriends_IsFollowing` (interface `SteamFriends017`), and correlates the asynchronous `FriendsIsFollowing_t` result (callback `345`) within a bounded timeout. It never calls `SteamAPI_Init` (no second init / DLL conflict) and resolves all Steam symbols at runtime, so **no Steamworks SDK is needed at build time**. Capability order: `steamworks.js` friends API → native addon → manual self-attest. When no automatic check is available (addon absent, Steam absent, or no logged-in user) `followCheckSupported` is `false`, the UI offers a persisted manual claim, and the launcher never fabricates a follow.

## Prerequisites

- **Windows 10/11 x64** with the **Steam client installed**.
- A **Steam account**: one that will follow the developer account, and the developer's **SteamID64**.
- **Visual Studio Build Tools** (Desktop development with C++) + **Python 3** + Node.js (repo version) + `node-gyp` (bundled with npm). No Steamworks SDK is required to build the addon.
- Repo checked out at the validated commit on `dev` (or a release tag).
- **Private config** (never committed): either `electron/steam-config.local.json` with `app_id` + `developer_steam_id` (copy the shape from `electron/steam-config.example.json`), or env vars `TCE_STEAM_APP_ID` / `TCE_STEAM_DEVELOPER_STEAM_ID`.
- A **test App ID the account can run** (e.g. `480` "Spacewar" for local dev) and a build/depot the account may publish to if using the SteamPipe path (Part C2).

## Part A — Build the native addon

1. Install JS deps at the repo root: `npm ci` (or `npm install`).
2. Build + stage the addon:
   ```
   npm run build:steam-friends
   ```
   - Runs `node-gyp rebuild` in `native/steam-friends` (targets the Node/Electron ABI).
   - Stages the binary as `node_modules/tce-steam-friends/build/Release/steam_friends.node`.
   - Expected output: `[steam] staged native friends addon at …`.
   - On a non-Windows host it warns and skips (expected).
3. Verify the staged module:
   - `node_modules	ce-steam-friends\build\Release\steam_friends.node` exists.
   - `node_modules	ce-steam-friends\package.json` has `"main": "build/Release/steam_friends.node"`.
   - *(Sanity only)* a bare `node -e "require('tce-steam-friends').init()"` returns `false` outside the launcher — expected, because `steam_api64.dll` is only loaded once `steamworks.js` initialises inside the Electron main process.

If `node-gyp` fails, fix the toolchain (MSVC workload / Python) and re-run; record the exact error.

## Part B — Build and package the Steam launcher

4. Install the optional SDK binding: `npm install steamworks.js`.
5. Package:
   ```
   npm run package:steam
   ```
   - Pre-flight runs `scripts/check-steamworks.mjs` then `scripts/check-steam-friends.mjs`; **both must pass on Windows**.
   - Produces the NSIS installer and `release\win-unpacked\` (the primary Steam artifact).
6. Confirm the addon was packed and unpacked from the asar, e.g.:
   - `release\win-unpackedesources\app.asar.unpacked
ode_modules	ce-steam-friends\build\Release\steam_friends.node`
   - If it is missing, the asar globs/`asarUnpack` in `electron-builder.yml` need fixing (record as a defect).

## Part C — Make it available in the local Steam client

Choose **C1** for a quick local pass, or **C2** for a true "installed from the Steam library" run.

### C1 — Add a Non-Steam Game (fast, no upload)

1. Start the Steam client and log in.
2. Library → **Add a Game** → **Add a Non-Steam Game…** → **Browse** → select `release\win-unpacked\Tableau Card Engine.exe` → **Add Selected Programs**.
3. Ensure the app learns a usable App ID: put `steam_appid.txt` containing the test App ID (e.g. `480`) next to the executable (or set `TCE_STEAM_APP_ID`), so `SteamAPI_Init` succeeds.
4. Launch the game **from the Steam library** (not from the filesystem) so a Steam user context exists.
5. Caveat: a non-Steam launch has no real App ID/ownership. `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` only needs a logged-in user context, but if `restartAppIfNecessary` causes a relaunch loop, use C2.

### C2 — SteamPipe dev build (real App ID, installed from the library)

1. Prepare SteamPipe config (never commit real IDs; keep them local):
   - `steam/app_build_<appid>.vdf`:
     ```vdf
     "AppBuild"
     {
       "AppID" "<appid>"
       "Desc" "TCE follow-detection validation"
       "BuildOutput" "..\build-output\"
       "ContentRoot" "..elease\win-unpacked\"
       "SetLive" "validation"
       "Preview" "0"
       "Local" ""
       "Depots"
       {
         "<depotid>"
         {
           "File" "depot_build_<depotid>.vdf"
         }
       }
     }
     ```
   - `steam/depot_build_<depotid>.vdf`:
     ```vdf
     "DepotBuild"
     {
       "DepotID" "<depotid>"
       "ContentRoot" "..elease\win-unpacked\"
       "FileMapping"
       {
         "LocalPath" "*"
         "DepotPath" "."
         "recursive" "1"
       }
       "FileExclusion" "*.pdb"
     }
     ```
2. Upload to a **beta branch** (leaves the default branch untouched):
   ```
   steamcmd +login <build_account> +run_app_build "..\steam\app_build_<appid>.vdf" +quit
   ```
3. In the Steam client: app **Properties → Betas → Beta Participation** → select `validation`.
4. **Install / Update** the app from the library and wait for the download to finish.
5. Launch from the library.

Verify the client is running the addon build (Part B step 6 path exists inside the install dir).

## Part D — Validation matrix

Record **Pass / Fail / N-A** and evidence (screenshot, console output, or note) for each row. UI/console helper: `await window.tce.steamFollow.supportsAutomaticFollowCheck()` via DevTools.

| # | Scenario | Steps | Expected |
|---|----------|-------|----------|
| D1 | Addon loaded / capability true | Logged in, following the dev account; open the follow CTA / call `supportsAutomaticFollowCheck()` | `true`; UI offers automatic detection; no crash |
| D2 | Automatic detection — positive | Follow the developer account, then trigger the follow re-check | Bonus (`bonusGameId` in `electron/bonus-catalog.json`, currently *Feudalism*) unlocks; **no manual claim** |
| D3 | Automatic detection — negative | Do **not** follow, then re-check | Bonus stays locked; no fabricated unlock |
| D4 | Not logged in | Steam running, no user logged in; launch | Boots; no crash; `isFollowing` returns `false`; bonus locked; manual claim available |
| D5 | Steam absent | Quit Steam; launch | Boots with a clear "Steam unavailable" warning; bonus locked; every non-gated game playable |
| D6 | Persistence | After a successful unlock, close and relaunch | Still unlocked; no re-prompt; no follow re-check on boot |
| D7 | Manual-claim fallback | Remove/rename `node_modules	ce-steam-friends` in the installed app; relaunch | `followCheckSupported === false`; manual self-attest claim still unlocks |
| D8 | Browser fallback | Open the web build in a plain browser | No bridge; nothing locked; app fully functional |
| D9 | Store page | Click "Follow us on Steam" | Store/community page opens inside the Steam client/overlay, already logged in; no crash |
| D10 | Regression (no Steam needed) | At the validated commit: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/steam-follow/`; `npm run build` | All green |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The addon builds on Windows x64 and `npm run package:steam` passes its pre-flights.
- [ ] The packaged artifact contains the unpacked `tce-steam-friends` `.node`.
- [ ] The launcher runs from the local Steam client with a logged-in account.
- [ ] With the account following the developer, `followCheckSupported === true` and the designated bonus unlocks automatically (no manual claim) — D1/D2.
- [ ] Not-logged-in and Steam-absent launches do not crash, do not fabricate a follow, keep the bonus locked, and keep base games playable — D4/D5.
- [ ] The unlock persists across relaunch without re-verification — D6.
- [ ] Manual-claim (D7), browser (D8) and store-page (D9) paths behave as specified.
- [ ] `tests/steam-follow/` unit tests and `npm run build` pass at the validated commit — D10.
- [ ] Evidence is recorded as a comment on this item, and the outcome is reflected on P6 `CG-0MUNBI08A001D0XU` and the parent `CG-0MUN7930Y009X8Z1`.

## Out of Scope

- Native addon builds for macOS/Linux (Windows x64 only).
- A publisher-backend / Steam Web API follow check.
- Steam achievements validation (separate epic).

- Completed validation matrix with evidence (screenshots / console / notes).
- A summary comment; any defects found become linked work items (blocking this item if they prevent a pass).

# 1916: The Rising — intake brief

## Problem statement

TCE has no example game that exercises **chronological sequencing / timeline
building** as a first-class mechanic, and none built around **researched
historical content** and **dialogue / encounter** mechanics. "1916: The Rising"
is the next single-player solitaire tableau game: the player, as a keeper of
memory, meets the spirits of Irish historical figures from the Norman invasion
(1169) to the Easter Rising (1916) and reconstructs the historical timeline by
meeting and talking to them.

## Users

- **Player (primary).** A single player who wants a short, thoughtful,
  solitaire session with a history/commemoration hook.
  - *As a player*, I want to meet a spirit and hear them speak, so that I learn
    who they were and when they lived.
  - *As a player*, I want to place a spirit correctly on the timeline, so that I
    feel I have understood their place in history.
  - *As a player who erred*, I want to retry or recover a misplacement, so that
    a single mistake does not end the session.
- **Engine maintainer / producer (secondary).** Wants a new game that pushes
  the engine forward with reusable, broadly applicable components (timeline /
  ordered-placement resolver, dialogue/encounter overlay, content-data layer,
  era/chronology helpers) and demonstrates the `MarketOfferEngine`, `Pile`,
  `HandView`, SLL, transcript, save/load and economy abstractions.
  - *As the producer*, I want the game registered in the distribution and the
    full quality gates green, so that it ships with the launcher.
- **Student / heritage learner (tertiary).** Could use the game as a light
  introduction to a named, sourced roster of figures across Irish history.

## Game concept (recommended design)

### Player fantasy

You are a *seanchaí* — a keeper of memory — who can sit with the spirits of
Ireland's past. The spirits will only speak to someone who listens. Reconstruct
the through-line of Irish history, from the first Norman landings to the Easter
Rising, by meeting each spirit and laying their testimony on the timeline.

### Core loop (one turn)

1. **Encounter** — a **Spirit Row** (market) offers N available spirits, drawn
   from era-grouped decks.
2. **Meet** — spend **Memory** to meet a spirit. A **Conversation** overlay
   opens.
3. **Converse** — choose one of 2–3 questions. Each answer yields a
   **testimony** (a first-person clue about the figure's era and deeds) and
   awards **Insight**.
4. **Place** — play the spirit card into the **Timeline** track. A placement is
   legal only when it preserves the relative chronological order of already
   placed anchors (Lost Cities-style ordered lanes, one shared line).
5. **Resolve** — a correct placement awards Insight and may award an **era
   bonus**; an illegal placement is rejected with feedback and the card stays in
   hand (or moves to a **Clouded** recovery area once per game).
6. **Clock** — after each round the **Rising clock** advances one decade-band.
   When it reaches 1916 the final chapter resolves.

### Win / loss

- **Win:** the full seven-chapter timeline is correctly ordered and Insight ≥
  the difficulty threshold before the clock reaches 1916.
- **Loss:** Memory is depleted with spirits still unplaced, or the clock
  reaches 1916 with the timeline incomplete / too many Clouded cards.

### Chapters (eras) of the timeline

1. **The Norman Landing & the Lordship** (1169–1300s) — Diarmait Mac Murchada,
   Aoife MacMurrough, Strongbow (Richard de Clare), Henry II, Ruaidrí Ua
   Conchobair.
2. **Gaelic Resurgence & the Tudor Conquest** (1400s–1603) — Art MacMurrough
   Kavanagh, Silken Thomas, Gráinne Mhaol (Grace O'Malley), Hugh O'Neill, Red
   Hugh O'Donnell.
3. **Plantation, Rebellion & Cromwell** (1603–1691) — the Flight of the Earls,
   the 1641 Rebellion, Patrick Sarsfield, the Treaty of Limerick.
4. **Penal Laws & the United Irishmen** (1691–1798) — Jonathan Swift, Wolfe
   Tone, Lord Edward FitzGerald, the 1798 Rebellion.
5. **Union, Emancipation & the Famine** (1801–1860s) — Daniel O'Connell,
   Catholic Emancipation, the Great Famine (1845–52), Young Ireland.
6. **Fenians, the Land War & Home Rule** (1860s–1913) — James Stephens, Michael
   Davitt, Charles Stewart Parnell, the Gaelic and literary revival.
7. **The Road to the Rising** (1913–1916) — the Dublin Lockout, the Irish
   Volunteers, the IRB Military Council, Patrick Pearse, James Connolly,
   Constance Markievicz, Tom Clarke, Joseph Plunkett.

> The roster is deliberately mixed-gender and spans Gaelic, Old English and
> Anglo-Irish figures; it is a *commemorative, source-backed* retelling, not a
> partisan one. Final roster is subject to content review (AC6).

### Mechanic reuse map (existing engine components)

| Mechanic | Reused component |
|---|---|
| Spirit row / market | `MarketOfferEngine` (`@card-system`) |
| Spirit / deck piles | `Pile<T>`, `createStandardDeck()`-style factories, seeded `shuffleArray()` |
| Player hand of met spirits | `HandView` (`@ui`) |
| Timeline track | SLL zones + a small ordered-track layout; `SpatialRules` only if adjacency bonuses are wanted |
| Placement legality | `LegalityResult` / `legalAction()` / `illegalAction()` (`@rule-engine`) |
| Memory economy | `EconomyLedger` (`@rule-engine`) |
| Undo a placement | `UndoRedoManager` + `CompoundCommand` (`@core-engine`) |
| Conversation overlay | `createOverlayBackground()` / `dismissOverlay()` / `createParameterizedOverlay()` (`@ui`) |
| Audio + feedback | `SoundManager`, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, `dealCard`/`flipCard`/`placeCard`/`popTextOrIcon`, reduced motion |
| Transcript + replay | `TranscriptRecorderBase`, `TranscriptStore`, `autoSaveTranscript()` |
| Save / resume | `SaveLoadStore`, `serializeWithVersion()`, `CheckpointManager` |
| Layouts | Screen Layout Language (`src/ui/screen-layout*.ts`) |
| Scene shell | `CardGameScene` |
| (Optional) achievements | `AchievementSystem` + `electron/achievement-manifest.json` mapping |

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC1 — Playable core loop.** From the Game Selector the player can start
"1916: The Rising", run a complete game, and reach both a win and a loss state,
with the loop Encounter → Meet → Converse → Place → Resolve → Clock executing
at least three full turns.

**AC2 — Timeline placement is legal only in correct relative chronological
order.** Placement is validated through `LegalityResult`; an out-of-order
placement is rejected with visible feedback and never mutates the timeline;
unit tests cover legal, illegal and boundary (first/last slot) placements.

**AC3 — Conversation mechanic.** Meeting a spirit opens a conversation that
returns a period clue/testimony; the same seed + same choices produce the same
clue sequence (deterministic), covered by a headless unit test.

**AC4 — All UI is SLL-driven.** Every scene layout is defined in
`src/layouts/rising.layout.json` and resolved through a `RisingLayoutAdapter`;
no hardcoded pixel positions for UI elements (card dimensions remain per-game
constants).

**AC5 — Feedback, accessibility and persistence.** Every player action that uses
a core animation helper is animated and sounded via `SoundManager` (no
double-play; `sfx-`-prefixed keys from `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`), reduced motion is
respected, a transcript recorder extends `TranscriptRecorderBase` and auto-saves,
and save/resume works via `SaveLoadStore` + `CheckpointManager`.

**AC6 — Historically accurate, sourced and respectful content.** Every spirit
card and testimony is drawn from published, citable sources; sources are listed
in the game's data file and attributed in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`; the
roster, language and framing pass an explicit content review (balance across
communities, no partisan or triumphalist framing, no glorification of
violence).

**AC7 — Quality gates, tests and docs.** Unit tests (`tests/the-rising/`) plus a
browser smoke test assert the scene boots and renders; the full project test
suite passes; `npm run build` succeeds; `README.md` game table,
`docs/DEVELOPER.md` game reference and the game's `help-content.json` are
updated.

**AC8 — Registered in the distribution.** The game is exported with `GAME_INFO`,
listed in `configs/full.json` and its own `configs/the-rising.json` preset,
discoverable as a sibling `../tce-the-rising` checkout, and navigable back to
the Game Selector via a `[ Menu ]` button.

## Constraints

- **Multi-repo:** the game lives in its own `tce-the-rising` repo (source at
  repo-root `src/`) composing the core as a `./core` submodule. The core repo
  carries no game; the core never submodules games.
- **Reuse first:** use the core components in the reuse map above. No bespoke
  hand/pile rendering (HandView/PileView + `flipCard()` are mandatory).
- **SLL is mandatory** for all UI layouts.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and in-game copy.
- **Licensing:** all assets must be permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0 or similar)
  and attributed in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- **Push to `dev` only** in both the core and the game repo; never `main`.
- **Content sensitivity:** handled as AC6; historical accuracy wins over
  gameplay convenience.

## Existing state

- No timeline/chronology example game exists. The closest precedents are **Lost
  Cities** (ordered expedition lanes — the nearest mechanic), **Main Street**
  (market row + tableau + economy + tutorial + transcript + challenges), **Sushi
  Go** (most recent reference implementation), and **Feudalism** (resource /
  adjacency tableau).
- The "create a new game" guidance is split between `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
  (§Adding an Example Game) and the `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` skill;
  the skill still describes the retired flat monorepo. A companion docs chore
  **CG-0MUZFNOE1007T57S** tracks consolidating/completing that guide; this epic
  is recorded as blocked-by it so the guide is corrected before implementation.
- `example-games/` in the core contains only the Gym.

## Desired change

Create the `tce-the-rising` example-game repo, implement the game described
above, register it in the distribution, and update all related documentation.

### Proposed delivery phases (for the plan skill to decompose)

1. **Content & data model** — spirit roster, eras, dates, testimonies, sources,
   data schema + validation.
2. **Pure game logic (headless)** — state, timeline legality, scoring,
   conversation selection, Memory economy, win/loss; unit tests first (TDD).
3. **Scene + SLL** — `RisingScene` (`CardGameScene`), SLL layout + adapter,
   renderer, animator, turn controller.
4. **Conversation overlay** — dialogue UI, options, testimony reveal.
5. **Polish & systems** — audio/SFX wiring, reduced motion, transcript, replay,
   save/load, checkpoints, undo/redo, difficulty presets, help panel.
6. **Registration, docs, assets, publication** — `GAME_INFO`, presets,
   README/DEVELOPER, CREDITS, thumbnail, fixture, repo scaffold + publish.

## Key Files (predicted)

New repo `../tce-the-rising` (source at repo-root `src/`):

- `src/TheRisingGame.ts` — pure game/session logic and state machine.
- `src/TheRisingRules.ts` — timeline placement legality + scoring.
- `src/TheRisingContent.ts` — spirit roster, eras, testimonies, sources.
- `src/TheRisingTranscript.ts` — transcript types + recorder.
- `src/TheRisingSaveLoad.ts` — versioned serializer.
- `src/createTheRisingGame.ts` — factory for browser tests.
- `src/layouts/rising.layout.json` — SLL layout document.
- `src/scenes/TheRisingScene.ts` — orchestrator (extends `CardGameScene`).
- `src/scenes/TheRisingLayoutAdapter.ts`, `TheRisingRenderer.ts`,
  `TheRisingAnimator.ts`, `TheRisingTurnController.ts`,
  `TheRisingOverlayContent.ts` — composable helpers.
- `src/scripts/adapters/TheRisingReplayAdapter.ts` — replay adapter.
- `src/scripts/generate-the-rising-fixture-transcript.ts` — fixture generator.
- `src/help-content.json`, `public/assets/the-rising/**`, `tests/the-rising/**`.

Core repo touch-points:

- `configs/full.json` and new `configs/the-rising.json` — preset registration.
- `README.md` — game table entry.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — game reference / smoke+dev profile tables.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — asset and source attribution.
- (Companion) `.pi/skills/tce-game-dev/SKILL.md` and the guide — see
  CG-0MUZFNOE1007T57S.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the game is single-player solitaire (no AI opponent). The
  concept describes meeting spirits, not competing with them.
- **Assumption:** timeline placement is *relative-order* enforcement (a puzzle),
  not free placement scored at the end.
- **Assumption (pending producer confirmation):** recommended answers to the
  three open design questions in Appendix A are accepted.
- **Risk — historical accuracy & sensitivity (high).** Mis-dating a figure or
  framing the material partisally would be a serious defect. *Mitigation:*
  cite published histories per card, run an explicit content review (AC6), and
  keep the framing commemorative.
- **Risk — content volume (medium).** A seven-era roster with testimonies is a
  lot of authored data. *Mitigation:* phase 1 delivers a minimal viable roster
  (≥3 spirits per era) and expands later; MVP separates content from logic.
- **Risk — timeline legality UX (medium).** A strict ordering puzzle can feel
  punishing. *Mitigation:* Clouded recovery area, hint affordance, difficulty
  presets, undo.
- **Risk — new-repo tooling (medium).** A new sibling repo needs scaffolding,
  preset wiring and publication. *Mitigation:* follow `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`
  and the DEVELOPER.md steps; verify with `npm run verify:runtime-plugin` if
  packaged as a runtime artifact.
- **Scope-creep:** a full Irish-history encyclopaedia, voice acting, localised

# F5: Scene interaction — HandView/PileView, card placement, drag-and-drop

## Summary
Wire up the interactive layer: Spirit Row cards (click to meet → move to hand), hand cards (click to select → move to placing phase), timeline slot clicks (click to place), and drag-and-drop support. Integrate with the game logic from F2/F3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Spirit Row interaction.** Clicking a card in the Spirit Row (market) checks Memory affordability. If affordable, the card moves to hand and opens the conversation overlay. If not affordable, illegal-move feedback is shown.

- **AC2 — Hand interaction.** Clicking a card in hand selects it for placement. The card is highlighted (selection lift via `HandView.setSelectionLift()`). Selecting a card switches the UI to "placing" mode.

- **AC3 — Timeline placement.** Clicking a timeline slot with a selected card validates the placement via `TheRisingRules.canPlaceFromHand()`. Legal placement animates the card to the slot, awards Insight, and advances the clock. Illegal placement shakes the card and shows feedback.

- **AC4 — Drag-and-drop.** Cards can be dragged from the Spirit Row directly to a timeline slot (buy-and-place). The same legality checks apply. Drag-and-drop is priced identically to the click path (no cheaper).

- **AC5 — Undo/redo.** A placed card can be undone via `UndoRedoManager` + `CompoundCommand`, returning the card to hand. Redo reinstates the placement.

## Minimal Implementation
- Integration of `HandView` for the hand of met spirits
- `PileView` for the Spirit Row (market) cards
- Timeline slot click handlers in `TheRisingTurnController.ts`
- Drag-and-drop handlers on Spirit Row and hand cards
- `UndoRedoManager` integration for undo/redo
- `shakeIllegalMove()` feedback on illegal placements

F4 (Scene shell + SLL) — provides the scene, layout, renderer, animator.

# F7: Polish - audio/SFX, transcript, save/load, undo, difficulty, help

## Summary
Wire up all the polish and systems: audio/SFX for every player action, transcript recording, save/load with checkpoints, undo/redo, difficulty presets, and the help panel.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 - Audio/SFX wiring.** Every player action that uses a core animation helper (dealCard, flipCard, placeCard, popTextOrIcon) is animated and sounded via SoundManager. SFX keys use COMMON_SFX_KEYS with sfx- prefix. No double-play. Reduced motion respects the mute flag.

- **AC2 - Transcript recording.** TranscriptRecorderBase is extended as TheRisingTranscript. Events recorded: spirit met, question chosen, placement attempted (legal/illegal), insight awarded, clock advanced, game end (win/loss). Transcript auto-saves on key events via autoSaveTranscript().

- **AC3 - Save/load.** SaveLoadStore + serializeWithVersion() / deserializeWithVersion() support saving and restoring game state. CheckpointManager provides autosave checkpoints at end-of-turn. Versioned deserialization fails on mismatch.

- **AC4 - Undo/redo.** UndoRedoManager + CompoundCommand support undoing the last placement and redoing it. The redo stack is invalidated after a new action (standard stack semantics).

- **AC5 - Difficulty presets.** At least 3 difficulty presets: Easy (more Memory, lower Insight threshold), Normal, Hard (less Memory, higher threshold, faster clock). The preset affects initial state values.

- **AC6 - Help panel.** HelpPanel is initialized with game-specific rules, controls, and win/loss conditions. The help text follows the Gym scene pattern (Features, Controls, Usage Example, Test Plan sections).

## Minimal Implementation
- Audio: SoundManager wiring in TheRisingAnimator + TheRisingScene
